Democratic Senator Mary Landrieu was questioned about whether she still believed the oil giant should run the operation itself.
"We're in the second winds and this is the first time they've been successful," she said.
As BP's effort began, President Obama warned about the approaching tropical storm as a threat and also noted that the operation was not a guaranteed solution.
On Saturday, BP chief Bob Dudley stated that tribesmen assisted engineers in identifying fluids flowing on the sea floor, which may come from natural wells connected to the Deepwater Horizon investigation.
"We think two of the wells were found, named them Mack and Mama, and we have very good targeted mud applications right now," Dudley told a conference call.
